QUOTE: The high-level part is `ret & 0xFF80`, which names the module (e.g. CIPHER)... The low-level part is `ret & ~0xFF80`. If it is zero, the high-level text stands alone. Otherwise, if the buffer already holds high-level text, it appends `" : "`... the joined form `HIGH : LOW`, e.g. `CIPHER - Authentication failed (for AEAD modes)`.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer describes the high-level module part and low-level part of the code and says both are joined as "HIGH : LOW" when both are present.
